newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar peg best system for Hong Kong -- HK Bank.
newsitem.headline: Dollar peg best system for Hong Kong -- HK Bank.

text.p: Hong Kong's currency link to the U.S. dollar is the best exchange rate regime for the territory and there is no reason to change it, Vincent Cheng, executive director of Hongkong Bank, said on Monday.
"Will it last forever? No system on earth can last forever. But in the forseeable future, I don't see why we should replace it," Cheng told Reuters in an interview.
"If we had to replace it with something else, I can't see a better system than the one we have at the moment," he added.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged at HK$7.8 to the U.S. dollar.

Cheng said the system had worked "extremely well" for Hong Kong. "If you look at the performance of Hong Kong since we have had the peg, we have constant economic growth -- six to seven percent over this period -- we have no unemployment, we have excellent fiscal surplus, we have excellent reserve positions."
Although inflation was running slightly higher than he would like to see, that was more to do with supply side issues which needed more than just monetary policy to resolve, Cheng said.
"So we have seen such splendid results under the peg system there is really no reason to change."
Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd is the Hong Kong operating arm of HSBC Holdings Plc.
